newsitem.title: USA: Smashing Pumpkins take center stage at MTV.
newsitem.headline: Smashing Pumpkins take center stage at MTV.

text.p: Alternative rockers Smashing Pumpkins took the spotlight on Wednesday at the annual MTV music video awards, winning seven prizes and making their first television appearance since the drug death of a keyboardist this summer.
In the 13th annual rock gala, broadcast live from landmark Radio City Music Hall, the Smashing Pumpkins took the honours for their animated sci-fi video "Tonight, Tonight."
The band suffered the heroin overdose death of keyboardist Jonathan Melvoin in July and the arrest of drummer Jimmy Chamberlin on drug charges. He was later fired from the band.
"We've had an interesting year. We lost a friend, we lost a drummer, but we hope we haven't lost any fans," lead singer, guitarist and songwriter Billy Corgan told the audience.
"To anyone who wonders, we're fine," he added.
Broadcast to 100 countries and hosted by comedian Dennis Miller, the MTV awards show has grown to rival the more established Grammy Awards.
The show was not without low points, particularly a live hook-up with the Russian Mir space station that proved disastrous with poor sound quality and a barely audible interpreter.
An obviously uncomfortable Miller quipped, "It's no wonder our two countries didn't get along for so long" before screaming an obscenity into the camera out of frustration.
But noticeably missing were showstopping events such as Michael Jackson's chaste kiss of his then-newlywed wife Lisa Marie Presley in 1994. The couple has since divorced.
The Smashing Pumpkins, which with eight nominations had the most of anyone, won video, direction, best alternative, best breakthrough, art direction, special effects and cinematography awards.
Corgan remarked later that he had little fondness for videos that now dominate the popular music industry.
"All videos ruin the song," he said. "They block the song into a mental image and for the rest of your life, you'll see that image with that song."

Canadian singer Alanis Morissette won best female artist, new artist and the editing award for "Ironic." The former child television actress, later a teen pop singer, released her Grammy-winning album "Jagged Little Pill" last year.

Morissette, introduced by actress Susan Sarandon who saluted the growing role of women in music, told the audience, "Although we women are coming into our own, we still love you men for what you are, just to let you know."

Rapper Coolio won best rap video and video from a film for his monster hit "Gangsta's Paradise" and best dance video for "1,2,3,4." The former convict and crack addict has become a spokesman for responsible music, singing about social issues.

Bush, a British alternative band, won the viewers choice award, determined by calls to an MTV phone number, for "Glycerine." Backstage, lead singer Gavin Rossdale said, "That's who we're playing for. They're the ones who care."

Alternative rock band the Foo Fighters won best group video for "Big Me," a parody of a Mentos candy commercial. Foo Fighters Dave Grohl and Pat Smear once played with Nirvana, which broke up after the suicide of lead singer Kurt Cobain.

The Fugees won the R&B award for "Killing Me Softly," a hip-hop remake of the 1973 hit by Roberta Flack. The band performed a medley that included "Ready or Not" from its album "The Score" and rapper Nas singing "If I Ruled the World."
